title: Crawler revamp, Phase 3, W1: listings onto the service
why: decisions/0160 W1 with its review fixes. The gate as Jason decided: a government page we read establishes a listing by itself; one other source does when the find scores past a line (Thresholds & gates, 'One source establishes a listing at', 50), shown as unconfirmed and checked continuously. OpenStreetMap is a lead, never a source (C11): it no longer counts toward the sources. A find the publish step would refuse (no street, town, state or ZIP) is no longer 'ready' and stuck in no list: it takes the second look, then reaches Review with what's missing (E23). Town jobs (E21): a lease that ran out isn't a try; failed jobs come back after 6 h, 1 day, 3 days; a partial job goes round at most 4 times; a town searched again after 30 days is looked at again, and for the kind searched when it isn't one of the town kinds; the coverage queue's own lease resets and retries run even when towns fill the hand-out; a coverage job cut short is no longer marked done. The place store (E23, C12): each read offers places never offered first (not the same first 40); a place with no kind is offered when its page gives a phone and a street; garbage, sanitation, refuse and the like are kinds' words; each source's use rule decides what shows and what becomes a find. Send the crawler uses its words (E22): a kind gets its own job in the town; a name is looked up by the crawler (a find_name request: one search from the month's paced allowance, then its own site). Search (E26): a business's name no longer teaches the site what kind its words mean ('blue hills' isn't propane), a name is read first in the directory, and the ?debug switch is gone. The worker's half (OpenStreetMap's phone, hours and street never copied without the business's own site; the find_name handler) deploys after this is live.
